glossary.definition: The agent that plans a task, sends pieces to worker agents and merges their results.
An agent started by another agent to do one piece of work in its own, fresh context.
Keeping each agent’s intermediate reading and tool calls out of other agents’ context windows.
Transferring ownership of a live conversation from one agent to another, exposed to the model as a tool.
The first agent in a support flow; it classifies the request and hands it to a specialist.
A shared store that several agents read from and write to, such as a typed graph state.
A function that says how a new update merges with a state key, for example appending to a list.
A record of which agent wrote an entry and from which source.
Agent2Agent, an open protocol for messages and tasks between separate agent systems.
Choosing the answer given by more than half of the agents.
An agent’s tendency to stick with its first answer even when it is wrong.
A rule that ends a multi-agent run, such as a message, token or time cap.
A taxonomy of 14 multi-agent failure modes in 3 categories, built from over 1,600 traces.
Elapsed real time from start to finish, as opposed to the total compute or tokens used.
Starting many independent pieces of work at once, then collecting and combining their results in one step.
The short, fixed-format result a sub-agent sends back, such as a card of at most 500 tokens, instead of its full transcript.
A fan-in step that compares results for shared figures, units, conflicts and gaps before they are combined.
The maximum number of sub-agents or calls allowed to run at the same time, often enforced with a semaphore.

symptomRouter.symptom: Is the work really parallel, or would one agent do?
symptomRouter.advice: Sketch the task graph, count independent branches, and split only if the time saved is worth about 15× the tokens.

symptomRouter.symptom: You want one agent to split a job into isolated pieces
symptomRouter.advice: Use an orchestrator with briefed, tool-scoped workers that return short summaries.

symptomRouter.symptom: A specialist should take over the conversation
symptomRouter.advice: Hand off with distinct descriptions, a typed payload and a cap on hops.

symptomRouter.symptom: Agents lose or overwrite each other’s findings
symptomRouter.advice: Type the shared state, add reducers, scope reads and record provenance.

symptomRouter.symptom: Would a second opinion catch errors, and is it worth the cost?
symptomRouter.advice: Start with majority voting over independent agents; add debate rounds only if they beat it.
Combine message, token and time caps with OR, detect repetition and verify before stopping.

symptomRouter.symptom: Many independent pieces take too long one after another, and one context cannot hold them all
symptomRouter.advice: Fan out one isolated sub-agent per piece, pass shared inputs in the brief, return cards of at most 500 tokens and run a merge check.
